facts.fact: The World Bank's results framework for the Digital Gabon Project reports 0 administrative departments with at least one civil registration office digitally registering vital acts, in a fully digitalised process ending with the birth record stored in the centralised civil registry database, at 31 May 2026, against a baseline of 0 in July 2021 and a target of 9 by June 2028.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)

facts.fact: The restructuring paper keeps Subcomponent 2.2, digitalisation of the civil registration system including birth registration, unchanged at US$10.5 million within a project closing on 30 June 2028, with three activities: mapping of archives and a feasibility study, technical assistance for a digitised civil registration system interoperable with the biometric population register, and kits, connectivity and building renovations; the date is the document's.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)

facts.fact: The civil registration digitalisation subcomponent (US$10.5 million) is financed from the World Bank IBRD loan for the Digital Gabon Project, net commitment US$64.10 million of which US$13.32 million (20.78 per cent) disbursed; the paper names no domestic budget line; the date is the document's.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)

facts.fact: The project's responsible agency is the state commission CN-TIPPEE, and the paper places data hosting for Component 2, which holds the civil registration system, at the Ministry of Interior's datacentre; the National Civil Registration Centre (CNEC) is not yet implemented, its implementation being an unmet disbursement condition; the date is the document's.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)

facts.fact: The World Bank states that a legal firm was recruited on 4 December 2025, to start in January 2026, on an integrated e-government legal framework that includes civil registration; the legal, regulatory and institutional framework for digitalised civil registration was still rated not implemented at 31 May 2026.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)

facts.fact: The World Bank reports a civil registration mapping exercise under way at 31 May 2026, to prioritise the departments whose offices will register digitally, with the project's technical assistance (AMOA) recruited in April 2026; no office was yet registering digitally.
facts.system: digitized CR system (Subcomponent 2.2, Digital Gabon Project)
